thread.title: UCLA defeats Iowa women's basketball team in Big Ten championship
thread.title_full: UCLA defeats Iowa women's basketball team in Big Ten championship

author: R. D. Martinez
title: UCLA defeats Iowa women's basketball team in Big Ten championship
text:
Iowa’s women’s basketball team, seeded second in the Big Ten Tournament, was defeated by top-seeded UCLA with a score of 96-45 on Sunday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. The loss moves Iowa to a season record of 26-6 overall and 15-3 in conference play, while UCLA advances to 31-1 overall and remains undefeated in the Big Ten.
The Hawkeyes struggled offensively from the start, trailing 22-5 after the first quarter. They made only two of their thirteen field goal attempts and committed seven turnovers during the opening period. Sophomore Taylor Stremlow led Iowa early with three points, including the team’s only three-pointer in that quarter.
By halftime, UCLA had extended its lead to 42-20. Sophomore Ava Heiden contributed seven points and three rebounds for Iowa during the first half, while Stremlow added six points. At halftime, Iowa was shooting just 25 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from beyond the arc.
UCLA continued to widen its margin through the third quarter, leading 67-36 after thirty minutes of play. Heiden scored six more points in that period for Iowa. In the final quarter, UCLA pulled further ahead to secure a decisive victory.
Heiden finished as Iowa’s top scorer with 15 points on 7-of-11 shooting and collected four rebounds. Freshman Addie Deal also reached double figures with eleven points and matched her career high by making three three-pointers. Sophomore Chit-Chat Wright added nine points along with five assists.
Overall, Iowa shot just under 28 percent from the field (17-of-61) and about 22 percent from three-point range (5-of-23). The team converted six out of eight free throws.
After the game, individual performances were noted: “Ava Heiden had a team-high 15 points (7-11 FG) and four rebounds.” The release also stated: “Heiden has reached double figures in 20 straight games and against all 17 Big Ten opponents played this season.” It continued: “Heiden has netted double figures in five consecutive Big Ten Tournament games dating back to last year.”
Taylor Stremlow contributed across multiple categories: “Taylor Stremlow notched six points, two assists, four rebounds, and two steals.” She also “made her ninth consecutive start and 16th of the year.” Chit-Chat Wright recorded “nine points, five assists, and four rebounds,” while Addie Deal registered “nine points (3-5 3FG), three assists, and a rebound.” It was noted that this was Deal’s sixth career game scoring in double digits.
From a team perspective: “Iowa has played six of the last eight Big Ten Tournament titles.” Coach Jensen is now “4-2 all-time in the Big Ten Tournament,” while since the start of the 2018–19 season Iowa holds an “18-4” record in tournament play.
Iowa will await its postseason fate during NCAA Tournament Selection Sunday on March 15 at 7 p.m. Central Time on ESPN.
summary: Iowa’s women’s basketball team, seeded second in the Big Ten Tournament, was defeated by top-seeded UCLA with a score of 96-45 on Sunday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. The loss moves Iowa to a season record of 26-6 overall and 15-3 in conference play, while UCLA advances to 31-1 overall and remains undefeated in the Big Ten. Freshman Addie Deal also reached double figures with eleven points and matched her career high by making three three-pointers.
